module: Old version (0.4) of the bananabench test bench, asynchronous: `benchPhysics` runs in a coroutine driven frame by frame (`coroutine.yield()` during gfxSteps = 20 frames), measuring by comparing dynamic collision enabled then disabled. Historical version, replaced by console/bananabench.lua.
notes: Code probably non-functional in 0.40.5: it does `require("lua/console/test")` (a file that does not exist in console/), uses `BeamEngine` as a global never defined here, and the old `BeamEngine:spawnObject` API (the new code uses spawnObject2).
The table `M = {}` is created globally (no `local`) and is not returned.
How it works: `benchmark_start()` creates the coroutine, `benchmark_update()` resumes it once (to be called on every engine update).
The per-vehicle results contain, for each vehicle count, two res entries (dynamic collision enabled/disabled) with beamspersec, percentRealtime, time and spawntime (in seconds).
For each measurement, a warm-up round is played then two measurements are accumulated (totalSteps = physicsSteps * 2 * gfxSteps).

myBenchStep.desc: Spawns vehicles up to n (positions 300*i), then lets gfxSteps frames pass (coroutine.yield) while measuring the time. Reports an instability.

n.desc: Number of vehicles to have in the scene.

benchLog.desc: Log collector: stores the entries (except levels A, D, S) in a local list and remembers the maximum severity (warn/error).

level.desc: Log level (A, D, S, W, E…).

benchPhysics.desc: Runs the benchmark (dynamic collision enabled then disabled) for each vehicle and returns the results table; must run in a coroutine.

benchmark_start.desc: Creates the coroutine that will run benchPhysics.

benchmark_update.desc: Resumes the coroutine by one step; to be called on every update by the host program.
